lessons.title: My Body
lessons.goal: Name the body in a clear head-to-feet order, then describe your own body.
lessons.known: Numbers; I have; this is my; personal pronouns; singular/plural.

scenes.face: Sofía identifies her own head and face in one consistent, natural portrait series. Show both eyes and both ears when counting; highlight only the intended part without hiding it. Include a clear nose detail between ears and mouth.
scenes.upper: Continue with the same Sofía. Frame the whole arms before a closer view of her hands; retain the same clothes and background. After the hands, show all ten fingers with thumb position clear and no hidden digits.
scenes.lower: Continue down the same body: full legs, then two visible feet. The actual phone crop must include both counted parts. After the feet, show all ten toes, unobstructed by footwear.
scenes.self: Return to a full view of Sofía and then Luis in a clearly introduced comparison. Use the visible speaker for first-person descriptions.

lessons.change: Adds nose, fingers and toes in their anatomical positions in every stage. The extra practice expands the lesson; no existing body target is removed to preserve the old count.

Listen.en: This is my head.
I have two eyes.
I have two ears.
This is my nose.
This is my mouth.
I have two arms.
I have two hands.
I have ten fingers.
I have two legs.
I have two feet.
I have ten toes.

lessons.title: How Are You?
lessons.goal: Ask how a person is, answer about that same person, then connect hunger and thirst to a request.
lessons.known: Family; be; I need; food and drinks; Can I have…?; polite service replies from Unit 5.

scenes.greet: Ana asks Luis how he is and he answers. Then Ana and Sofía discuss a clearly indicated girl: she always refers to that same girl. The two adults are the questioner and respondent; the girl is not made to describe herself as she.
scenes.rest: Ana asks Sofía about the established grandfather after his walk. Both look toward the same grandfather; Sofía answers about him, with a matched closer answer view.
scenes.food: Ana asks the baby’s parent how the baby is. The parent answers; the baby never speaks the third-person line. A subsequent food request has its own customer, server, handover and receipt.
scenes.water: Luis is thirsty after the walk. He requests water from that server, receives it and thanks them. Keep cup ownership consistent.

lessons.change: Every Learn answer now has its question, with the baby, grandfather and she forms explicitly modelled. The referent stays constant across both turns. Speak and Use give the question and answer their own adjacent cards.

lessons.title: My Clothes
lessons.goal: Name clothes, describe their colors and identify whose clothes they are.
lessons.known: Colors; this/these; my/his/her; have; known people and object-location language.

scenes.main: Sofía and Luis lay out their separate clothes on two clearly identified chairs. Introduce shirt/pants, then a separate dress/skirt comparison. Do not assume all alternatives belong to one outfit.
scenes.layer: The same pair compare jackets, then hats. A color contrast uses the same garment and composition with only color changed.
scenes.feet: Sofía’s socks and shoes appear as complete pairs, first separately and then with their owner. Do not hide one shoe or sock.
scenes.belong: Finish by matching each established person with their visible belongings; a pointing speaker identifies ownership.

lessons.change: Retain all eight clothing targets and carry their order through every stage. Use color and possession for growth; wearing/put on/take off are not silently added.

lessons.title: The Weather Today
lessons.goal: Ask how the weather is today, answer with sky and temperature, then combine the facts.
lessons.known: It is; and; today; days; in the morning/afternoon.

scenes.sky: Two explicitly separate days in the same neighborhood: a clear sunny view followed by a cloudy view. They are comparisons, not a sudden unexplained weather change.
scenes.rain: Continue the weather comparison with visible rain, then a windy tree-and-clothing scene. Cloudiness alone cannot prove rain or wind.
scenes.temperature: Compare a cold morning and a hot afternoon. Use visible human/environmental temperature evidence; sunshine alone cannot establish hot.
scenes.combine: Return to two established moments: a cold, windy morning and a hot, sunny afternoon. Keep the visual facts consistent.

lessons.change: Adds “How is the weather today?” as an explicit question-and-answer model, listening exchange, spoken question and sentence construction. Separate days and places make contrasting weather truthful.

lessons.title: What I Like to Do
lessons.goal: Say which activities you like, ask a friend about theirs, and discover a shared interest.
lessons.known: Earlier I like / I do not like, Do you…?, Yes, I do / No, I do not; people, places and times. Teach the complete activity phrases here before invitations use their base forms.

scenes.home: A conversation about free time at home. Ana states that she likes to watch TV; Luis states that he likes to listen to music. Those utterances establish preferences. Recognition options illustrate activities, not whether a photographed person likes them.
scenes.create: Friends share creative interests in order: dance, draw, paint. Drawing is clearly pencil on paper; painting clearly uses a brush and paint. The correct image depicts the named activity only; the heard or written speaker supplies I like to.
scenes.outside: The same conversation turns to outdoor interests: ride a bike, take photos, play football. Use clearly safe cycling, an obvious camera/photography action, and association football with a visible football. Teach bike and photos as part of their full phrases.
scenes.share: Sofía asks Ana about football; Ana says no. Luis asks Ana about photos; she says yes. These are coherent different preferences. Invitations follow in 7.7, not in this lesson.

lessons.change: Replaces the current-action detour with I like to… in every stage. Adds dance, draw, paint, ride a bike, take photos and play football alongside watch TV and listen to music. No repeated reading/swimming/playing action-label cards. Recognize matches the activity explicitly named in a preference; it never guesses a preference from a photograph.

lessons.title: Please Repeat
lessons.goal: Repair a misunderstanding, hear the information again and use it to reach a destination.
lessons.known: Help and polite openings from 6.10; bus/ticket/times from 6.11–6.12; directions and destinations; thanks. I need help is retrieved, not labelled new.

scenes.ask: Ana is at the station and needs the bus to the museum. A uniformed helper is visibly available; retain Ana and this helper throughout the exchange.
scenes.repeat: The helper gives the bus information. Ana asks for repetition; the helper repeats the same correct information without changing the destination or bus.
scenes.confirm: The repeated answer identifies the blue bus and nine o’clock. A timetable/clock and matching vehicle make the result visible. The timetable answer is initially delivered naturally but quicker than Ana can follow. Her request produces the same nine-o’clock answer more clearly; never change the time during repair.
scenes.slow: At the museum stop, a different, explicitly introduced helper gives the last walking directions. Ana requests slower speech, hears the same route clearly and thanks them. The contrast is in actual speech rate, not a blurry picture or a gesture. Prepare two natural takes with identical route wording; do not stretch phonemes or make the first take unintelligible.
scenes.arrive: Ana follows that exact route and reaches the museum. Keep her clothes, bag and museum architecture consistent through departure and arrival.

lessons.change: Adds fast inside “You speak fast.” and “You speak fast. Please speak slowly.” The before/after speech pace must be audible; a static image cannot prove fast or slowly. The helper repeats the same information at a clear, natural pace and Ana uses it.

lessons.goal: Retrieve the expanded body, clothing, weather, preference and repair language through fresh everyday situations.
lessons.known: All language has already been introduced. Fresh people and images; no new vocabulary.
arc: Find the place and solve a misunderstanding

scenes.ready: Fresh cast: Diego prepares for a cold outing. A body-identification mirror sequence establishes the head-to-toe map, then fingers and toes motivate gloves and boots. A packing scene names a coat, sweater and scarf. Separate sunny/hot and rainy transfers are explicitly labelled, never sudden weather changes. All photographs are new review material.
scenes.friends: A separate visit with Sofía and friends. Questions identify exactly whose feeling is discussed; food and water needs receive a response. They share indoor, creative and outdoor interests, then decline football and agree on music. Each preference comes from an utterance, never a guessed facial expression.
scenes.route: A different visitor travels to the park. They check a time, ask for repetition and slower directions, then reach the friends. Keep this encounter internally continuous.

lessons.change: The review grows to retrieve the new body parts, weather question, clothing and hobbies, plus fast. Preferences use I like to… throughout. Added cards retain the three coherent stations and do not introduce assessed language.

lessons.title: Mission: A Day with Friends
lessons.goal: Prepare, travel, solve a misunderstanding and join friends at the park.
lessons.known: All Units 1–7; no new assessed language.
lessons.change: The same outing now begins with the weather question, uses the new clothing and finger vocabulary, repairs fast speech, and carries a new hobby into a shared activity. Fifteen listening scenes precede the four closing voice tasks.

beats.title: Check today’s weather
beats.scene: Before choosing what to take, Ana asks Luis about today’s weather at home. His answer establishes the cold, rainy outing; both speakers have distinct views.

beats.title: Prepare for the weather
beats.scene: Ana prepares for the same cold, rainy trip. Four distinct targets show the speaker indicating her cold fingers, her pair of gloves, her winter coat and her boots. Later views retain these belongings.

beats.title: Leave with what you need
beats.scene: Four connected moments follow Ana, wearing the same clothes and carrying the same umbrella and bag, from home to the stop.

I am going to the park.
First, I walk to the bus stop.
Then, I am at the bus stop.
cues.target: Visible arrival at the same stop

beats.title: Find the right bus
beats.scene: Ana asks a helper at the stop. Exactly two visible speaking roles; the response identifies the bus.

cues.en: Which bus goes to the park?
The blue bus goes to the park.

beats.title: Ask again
beats.scene: Ana did not understand; the same helper repeats the same destination and bus.

cues.en: I do not understand. Please repeat.
The blue bus goes to the park.

beats.title: Get the ticket
beats.scene: At the counter, Ana requests a ticket; the agent hands it over. Ticket ownership changes visibly.

cues.en: Can I have a ticket, please?

beats.title: Check departure
beats.scene: Ana asks departure time; the agent indicates a clock/timetable showing nine.

cues.en: What time does the bus leave?

beats.title: Check arrival
beats.scene: Same service, a different arrival field/time; leave and arrive are never swapped.

cues.en: What time does the bus arrive?

beats.title: Ride to the park stop
beats.scene: Four consecutive travel moments keep the same Ana, bus, ticket and destination. The bus arrives before she gets off.

cues.en: First, I get on the blue bus.
Then, I get off the bus.

beats.title: Clarify and follow the route
beats.scene: Visible Spanish setup establishes that Ana could not follow the directions. Two speaking roles at the stop: Ana requests slower speech and the helper gives the route clearly. A non-assessed scene transition then shows Ana walking straight, turning left and reaching the park with the same belongings.

cues.en: You speak fast. Please speak slowly.

cues.target: Helper repeats the previously established route clearly

beats.title: Meet everyday needs
beats.scene: At the park café, needs cause a request, handover and thanks. Four linked scene moments keep the customer, server and drink consistent.

cues.en: I am thirsty. I need water.

beats.title: Invite a friend
beats.scene: At the park, Sofía invites Luis. His visible tired state is context; the heard refusal establishes the actual reply.

cues.en: Do you want to play football?

beats.title: Offer an alternative
beats.scene: Same people and time. Music is a suitable alternative to active play.

cues.en: Do you want to listen to music?

beats.title: Include another friend
beats.scene: Ana shares her interest in photography at the park; her friend proposes doing it together. The next scene visibly shows them taking photos before the later meeting is agreed.

beats.title: Agree on the next meeting
beats.scene: After the activity, the friends agree on a later day. They remain together at the park.

cues.target: Sofía suggests a future activity through the taught invitation chunk
